# @n3wth/ui

> The shared Newth brand and page system, built on Astryx primitives.

## Architecture

Dependencies flow from Sites to @n3wth/ui to Astryx.

- Sites own content, routes, product state and business logic.
- @n3wth/ui owns the Newth theme, fonts, navigation, page headers, sections, footer and compatibility adapters.
- Astryx (@astryxdesign/core) supplies native primitives and their interaction behavior.
- Applications consume Astryx through UI's primitives facade instead of creating another direct dependency.

## Workspace entry points

These paths describe the current repository. They do not establish that the same exports are already available in a published npm version.

- @n3wth/ui/site: N3wthProvider, SiteNavigation, PageHeader, SiteContainer, SiteSection, SiteHeading, SiteText and SiteFooter.
- @n3wth/ui/primitives: native Astryx component APIs, plus ToastViewport.
- @n3wth/ui/site.css: shared Newth theme, fonts and site component styles.
- @n3wth/ui/tailwind-theme.css: UI facade for the Astryx Tailwind theme bridge.
- @n3wth/ui: existing compatibility APIs and project-specific utilities. Do not mix their props with native primitive props.
- @n3wth/ui/styles: compatibility CSS used by existing consumers.

## Build a site

From the repository root, use Node 24 and npm 11.19.1:

```bash
npm ci
npm run site:new -- my-idea "My idea"
npm install
npm run build --workspace @n3wth/ui
npm run check --workspace @n3wth/my-idea
npm run check:design
```

The starter creates source files, not a deployment or domain. Replace its copy before publishing.

## Shared presentation

- Satoshi headings, Geist Sans body text, Geist Mono code.
- Five semantic text roles: page, section, item, body and supporting.
- Router links and callbacks remain in the app.
- Shared site components own ordinary width, spacing and navigation behavior.
- Route content appears immediately. Use motion only for deliberate product demonstrations or functional feedback.
- Preserve labels, keyboard access, focus indicators, text contrast and reduced-motion behavior. Validate the actual page; library adoption alone does not prove accessibility compliance.
